trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Lisbon, Portugal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour
experiences.description: Spend a few hours grazing through Lisbon's iconic food market featuring the best local chefs and traditional dishes. Sample bacalhau (salt cod), pastéis de nata, bifanas, and regional cheeses while mingling with locals and learning about Portuguese culinary traditions.

experiences.name: Belém Historical Landmarks & Pastéis de Belém
experiences.description: Visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery and the iconic Tower of Belém, both masterpieces of Manueline architecture dating to the Age of Discovery. Finish with a visit to the original Pastéis de Belém bakery, open since 1837, for the world-famous custard tarts.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight TP lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled. Take the Aerobus or Metro (Red Line) from Lisbon Airport to the city centre for around €2–€4, a budget-friendly alternative to taxis.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Lisbon City Stay, then take a leisurely walk to explore the surrounding neighbourhood. Head to Praça do Comércio (Commerce Square) and stroll along the Tagus riverfront promenade — both completely free. Get oriented with the city layout and soak in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Wander uphill into the Alfama district, Lisbon's oldest neighbourhood. Explore the narrow cobblestone streets, admire the colourful azulejo tiles on building facades, and enjoy views over the city from the Portas do Sol viewpoint (miradouro) — all free of charge.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick pastel de nata (custard tart) and a bica (espresso) at the airport or a nearby café upon arrival — budget around €2–€3.
meals.lunch: Pick up a prego (steak sandwich) or bifana (pork sandwich) from a local tasca near the hotel for €3–€5.
meals.dinner: Try a simple but hearty meal at a neighbourhood tasca in Alfama. Look for the prato do dia (dish of the day) which typically includes soup, main, and bread for €8–€10. Cervejaria Ramiro area has affordable options, or ask locals for the nearest 'menu do dia'.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a 24-hour Viva Viagem transport card (€0.50 card + €6.40 for 24h unlimited) if you plan to use trams and metro frequently. Keep arrival day light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Exchange a small amount of cash or use ATMs (avoid airport exchange desks for better rates).

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a visit to the São Jorge Castle (Castelo de São Jorge). Arrive early to beat crowds. Entry is €15 for adults, but the walk up through Alfama's winding streets is free and scenic. Enjoy panoramic views over Lisbon's terracotta rooftops and the Tagus River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour experience — spend a few hours grazing through Lisbon's iconic food market at Mercado da Ribeira. Sample dishes from the best local chefs and traditional food stalls. This is a fantastic way to try multiple local specialities (petiscos) without committing to a full restaurant meal. Budget €15–€20 for a satisfying food crawl.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to the Bairro Alto neighbourhood for a relaxed evening. Browse the bohemian streets, pop into local ginjinha (cherry liqueur) bars — a tiny shot glass costs just €1.50. Enjoy the lively but affordable street atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Start at a local padaria (bakery) near the hotel — coffee and pastel de nata for €2–€3.
meals.lunch: The Time Out Market is your lunch — graze on petiscos, fresh seafood, and local bites. Budget €15–€20 total.
meals.dinner: Find a traditional tasca in Bairro Alto for bacalhau à brás (shredded salted cod with eggs and potatoes) or caldo verde (kale soup). A full meal with house wine costs €10–€14.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday mornings at the Time Out Market are lively — go before 1pm to avoid the biggest crowds. The market is located in Cais do Sodré, easily reachable by tram or a 20-minute walk from Alfama. Wear comfortable shoes — Lisbon's hills are steep and cobblestones can be tricky.

day_by_day.morning: Take the iconic Tram 28E (€3 single ticket or included in transport pass) for a scenic ride through historic neighbourhoods including Graça, Alfama, and Estrela. This is one of Lisbon's most famous experiences and doubles as both transport and sightseeing. Hop off at Basílica da Estrela for a look at this stunning 18th-century baroque church — entry is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Belém Historical Landmarks experience. Head to Belém by tram or bus (included in transport pass). Visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery (€10 entry, or free on Sunday mornings before 2pm — check current policy) and the iconic Tower of Belém (€6 entry), both masterpieces of Manueline architecture. Walk along the Belém waterfront and visit the Monument to the Discoveries for free from the outside.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at the famous Pastéis de Belém bakery (the original since 1837) for a warm, freshly baked pastel de Belém dusted with cinnamon — just €1.50 each. Then return to the city centre and relax at a miradouro (viewpoint) such as Miradouro da Graça for a peaceful sunset.

meals.breakfast: Sunday treat — enjoy a full breakfast at a local café near the hotel: toast, eggs, juice, and coffee for €5–€7.
meals.lunch: Grab a simple lunch near Belém — try a tasca along Rua de Belém for grilled fish or a sandwich. Budget €8–€12.
meals.dinner: Head to Mouraria neighbourhood for affordable and diverse dining. Try a traditional Portuguese cozido à portuguesa (meat and vegetable stew) or arroz de marisco (seafood rice). Budget €10–€13 with a glass of house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Check opening hours for Jerónimos Monastery in advance — Sunday free entry (before 2pm) can mean longer queues. Belém is about 6km from the city centre; Bus 714 or 727 from Praça do Comércio is the most budget-friendly option. Bring a light jacket as the Tagus riverfront can be breezy.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Mouraria neighbourhood, Lisbon's multicultural heart and the birthplace of fado music. Visit the free Fado Museum (Museu do Fado) — entry is €5, very worthwhile for understanding this UNESCO-recognised music tradition. Wander the neighbourhood's colourful streets and street art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museu Nacional do Azulejo (National Tile Museum) — entry is €5 and it's one of Lisbon's most unique and underrated museums. Explore centuries of Portuguese azulejo tile art, including a stunning 23-metre panoramic tile panel of pre-earthquake Lisbon (1755). Easily reachable by bus 794 or a short taxi ride.
day_by_day.evening: Experience live fado music — Lisbon's soulful traditional music genre. Many restaurants in Alfama offer free fado performances in the evening with dinner. Look for tascas advertising 'fado vadio' (amateur fado nights) which are free or very low cost. Alternatively, the Fado in Chiado area has affordable options.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and tosta mista (ham and cheese toast) at a local café — €3–€4.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local workers' restaurant (restaurante económico) in Mouraria for a full menu do dia — soup, main course, dessert, and drink for €8–€10.
meals.dinner: Choose a fado restaurant in Alfama with dinner included — budget €15–€20 for a set dinner with live music. Alternatively, eat cheaply beforehand (€8–€10) and pay a small cover charge for a fado vadio venue.

day_by_day.notes: Monday can mean some museums are closed — the Azulejo Museum and Fado Museum are typically open, but always verify hours in advance. Fado vadio nights are authentic and budget-friendly — ask your accommodation host for recommendations on the best local spots. Carry cash as smaller tascas may not accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Feira da Ladra flea market in Campo de Santa Clara (open Tuesday and Saturday mornings, free entry). Browse stalls selling vintage items, antiques, books, and local curiosities. A great place to find affordable souvenirs and experience local life. Nearby Igreja de São Vicente de Fora has beautiful azulejo-lined cloisters (€5 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a free walk through Príncipe Real neighbourhood — one of Lisbon's most charming areas with a weekend antique market, beautiful gardens (Jardim do Príncipe Real), and elegant 19th-century architecture. Visit the Jardim Botânico de Lisboa (Botanical Garden) for €3 entry — a peaceful green escape in the city.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Lisbon — return to a favourite neighbourhood for a farewell dinner. Splurge slightly on a traditional Portuguese seafood dish such as grilled sea bass (robalo) or percebes (barnacles) at a local restaurant. Toast with a glass of vinho verde (young Portuguese wine) or a ginjinha.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at the Feira da Ladra market area — fresh fruit, pastries, or a café nearby for €3–€5.
meals.lunch: Try a bifana or prego sandwich with a beer at a local snack bar in Príncipe Real — €5–€7.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a traditional tasca — budget €15–€18 for a full meal with wine. Ask locals or your accommodation host for their personal recommendation for the most authentic spot.

day_by_day.notes: Pack and prepare for departure the following day. Keep receipts for any VAT refund eligibility on purchases. The Aerobus or Metro Red Line back to the airport costs €2–€4 and takes about 20–30 minutes — much cheaper than a taxi. Lisbon's tap water is safe to drink, saving money on bottled water throughout the trip. Total estimated daily budget (excluding accommodation): €35–€55 per day including transport, entry fees, and meals.

trip_options.title: Classic Lisbon, Portugal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.description: Explore Lisbon's oldest neighborhood on a guided walking tour through narrow medieval alleyways, visiting São Jorge Castle and the Sé Cathedral. End the evening at a traditional Fado house for an authentic Portuguese music experience paired with local wine.

experiences.name: Sintra Royal Palaces Day Trip
experiences.description: Take a short train ride to the fairy-tale town of Sintra and explore the colorful Pena Palace and the mysterious Moorish Castle perched on forested hilltops. Discover centuries of Portuguese royal history while enjoying panoramic views of the Atlantic coastline.

experiences.name: Mouraria Neighborhood Food & Culture Walk
experiences.description: Wander through Lisbon's multicultural Mouraria quarter, the birthplace of Fado, on a self-guided or small-group culinary walk. Taste petiscos (Portuguese tapas) at traditional tascas, visit the vibrant Intendente Square, and discover the rich Moorish heritage woven into the neighborhood's streets and tiles.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the Aerobus or Metro (Red Line to Green Line) to Lisbon City Stay. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with a neighborhood stroll around the hotel area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Time Out Market Lisbon (Mercado da Ribeira) for a relaxed first taste of the city. Graze through stalls from top local chefs — try the bacalhau croquettes, grilled octopus, and a glass of Vinho Verde. This iconic market is the perfect low-key introduction to Lisbon's food scene after a long journey.
day_by_day.evening: Take a gentle walk along the Ribeira waterfront promenade to soak in views of the Tagus River and the 25 de Abril Bridge at golden hour. End the evening with a quiet dinner at a traditional tasca near the Cais do Sodré area.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastel de nata at the airport or skip — arrival is at 13:00.
meals.lunch: Time Out Market Lisbon — budget €15–20 per person grazing multiple stalls. Try the bifanas, fresh seafood, and local cheeses.
meals.dinner: Taberna da Rua das Flores or a similar traditional tasca near Cais do Sodré — expect €25–35 per person for petiscos (Portuguese tapas), grilled fish, and a carafe of house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. The Time Out Market requires no reservation and is open until midnight, making it very flexible for arrival day. Get a 24-hour Metro Viva Viagem card (€1.50 card + top-up) at the airport for easy transport.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a classic Lisbon breakfast at a neighborhood café — coffee and pastéis de nata. Then embark on the Alfama District Walking Tour, beginning at the Portas do Sol viewpoint (miradouro). Wander through narrow medieval alleyways, discover hidden courtyards, and visit the Sé de Lisboa (Lisbon Cathedral), one of the city's oldest landmarks dating to 1147.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Alfama by visiting the National Pantheon (Panteão Nacional) and the Church of São Vicente de Fora for sweeping rooftop views over the city and river. Browse the Sunday Feira da Ladra flea market (runs until ~18:00) for vintage finds, antiques, and local curiosities — a beloved Lisbon tradition.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Alfama for the Fado Show experience — book a dinner-and-fado package at a reputable casa de fado such as Mesa de Frades or Tasca do Chico. Arrive by 20:00 for dinner, and experience live Fado music, Portugal's soulful and UNESCO-listed musical tradition, in an intimate setting.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria near the hotel — espresso and pastel de nata for €2–3. Try Confeitaria Nacional if near Rossio.
meals.lunch: Tasca do Simão or a simple local restaurant in Alfama — grilled sardines, bread, and salad for €12–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Casa de Fado dinner (e.g., Tasca do Chico or Mesa de Frades) — €35–50 per person including dinner and the Fado show. Reservation strongly recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Alfama's cobblestone hills are steep. The Feira da Ladra flea market only runs on Tuesdays and Saturdays/Sundays. Book the Fado dinner show at least 2–3 days in advance as seats are limited. Alfama is easily walkable from most central Lisbon hotels.

day_by_day.morning: Take the commuter train from Cais do Sodré station (€2.35 each way) for the 40-minute journey to Sintra. Arrive by 09:30 to beat the crowds. Head straight up to the colorful Pena Palace (Palácio da Pena), a 19th-century Romanticist castle perched on the hilltop with stunning views over the forested Serra de Sintra. Explore the palace interiors and surrounding parkland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the shuttle bus down to the historic Sintra Vila (town center) and visit the Sintra National Palace (Palácio Nacional de Sintra), recognizable by its twin conical chimneys — one of Portugal's best-preserved medieval royal palaces. Stroll the charming town streets, pop into artisan shops, and try local sweets like travesseiros (puff pastry with egg cream) and queijadas.
day_by_day.evening: Return by train to Lisbon (trains run frequently until late evening). Enjoy a relaxed dinner back in Lisbon in the Príncipe Real or Bairro Alto neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Quick café breakfast near Cais do Sodré before boarding the train — croissant and galão coffee for €3–4.
meals.lunch: Saudade restaurant or Tascantiga in Sintra town center — local soup, meat or fish dish, and dessert for €15–22 per person.
meals.dinner: Taberna da Esquina or Bairro do Avillez in Bairro Alto/Príncipe Real — modern Portuguese cuisine, €28–40 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: Buy train tickets at Cais do Sodré station (Linha de Sintra). Pena Palace tickets should be booked online in advance (€14 palace + park, or €8 park only) — queues can be very long. Wear layers as Sintra can be cooler and mistier than Lisbon. The full day trip is approximately 8–9 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Take Tram 15E or a rideshare to Belém (20–30 minutes from the city center). Begin with the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery (Mosteiro dos Jerónimos), a masterpiece of Manueline architecture built in the 16th century to celebrate Vasco da Gama's voyage to India. Explore the ornate cloisters, the church, and the tombs of Vasco da Gama and Luís de Camões. Arrive early (opening at 10:00) to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the waterfront to the iconic Tower of Belém (Torre de Belém), another UNESCO Manueline gem jutting into the Tagus River. Visit the Monument to the Discoveries (Padrão dos Descobrimentos) and climb to the top for panoramic views. Stop at the legendary Pastéis de Belém bakery (the original since 1837) for the world-famous custard tarts, dusted with cinnamon and powdered sugar — a non-negotiable Lisbon experience.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward central Lisbon and explore the Mouraria Neighborhood Food & Culture Walk — Lisbon's multicultural quarter and the historic birthplace of Fado. Wander through the lively streets, visit the Intendente square, and sample street food from the diverse international community that calls Mouraria home.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hotel — coffee and toast (tosta mista) for €3–5.
meals.lunch: Pastéis de Belém (Rua de Belém 84) — enjoy the famous custard tarts (€1.20 each) alongside a bica coffee, plus a light snack. Or sit down at Solar dos Presuntos nearby for a heartier meal at €18–25.
meals.dinner: Tasca do Chico or a Mouraria neighborhood restaurant such as Zé da Mouraria — hearty Portuguese home cooking, €20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Jerónimos Monastery is closed on Mondays — Tuesday is perfect. Book monastery tickets online (€10) to skip the queue. The Pastéis de Belém bakery can have a line but moves quickly — takeaway is fastest. Belém is best explored in the morning before tour groups arrive. The Mouraria walk in the evening is relaxed and safe — the neighborhood has been beautifully revitalized.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a leisurely final morning exploring the Chiado and Príncipe Real neighborhoods — Lisbon's most elegant and bohemian quarters. Visit the historic Livraria Bertrand (world's oldest operating bookshop, est. 1732), browse the independent boutiques and antique shops along Rua Dom Pedro V, and relax in the Jardim do Príncipe Real garden. Visit the Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga (National Museum of Ancient Art) if you want a cultural morning — one of Portugal's finest art collections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Bairro Alto area and take the iconic Elevador da Glória or Elevador da Bica funicular for a classic Lisbon experience. Enjoy the views from the Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara viewpoint. Spend the afternoon doing any last-minute souvenir shopping — look for azulejo tiles, ginja liqueur, tinned sardines, and Portuguese wine. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a special farewell dinner at a restaurant that encapsulates everything you've loved about Lisbon — great food, warm atmosphere, and Portuguese hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Café A Brasileira in Chiado (est. 1905, a Lisbon institution) — coffee and pastries in a beautiful art deco setting for €4–6.
meals.lunch: Mercado de Campo de Ourique (a more local, less touristy food market) — fresh, varied, and budget-friendly at €12–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Alma (Chef Henrique Sá Pessoa, Chiado) or Cervejaria Ramiro for spectacular shellfish and seafood — €40–55 per person for a memorable final meal. Reservation required.

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight departure time and plan accordingly — if departing the next morning, keep the evening relaxed. Cervejaria Ramiro (seafood) is a legendary Lisbon institution and does not take reservations — arrive before 19:00 or expect a wait. The Elevador da Bica and Elevador da Glória are covered by the standard Metro/transport card. Allow 45–60 minutes to reach the airport from the city center.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private transfer arranged from Humberto Delgado Airport to Lisbon City Stay hotel. Settle in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity in your luxury suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely stroll through the elegant Chiado and Baixa districts near the hotel. Explore Praça do Comércio along the Tagus riverfront, admire the iconic Arco da Rua Augusta, and soak in your first impressions of Lisbon at a relaxed pace. Visit the historic Livraria Bertrand, the world's oldest operating bookshop.
day_by_day.evening: Alfama District Walking Tour & Fado Show — join a premium guided evening tour through Lisbon's oldest medieval neighborhood, winding through narrow cobblestone alleys, past ancient miradouros (viewpoints), and into a traditional Fado house for an intimate, soul-stirring live Fado performance with wine and petiscos included.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — mid-day arrival. Enjoy a light welcome snack at the hotel upon check-in.
meals.lunch: Taberna da Rua das Flores — a beloved Lisbon tavern near Chiado serving elevated Portuguese petiscos and seasonal small plates with a curated natural wine list. Ideal for a first taste of authentic local cuisine.
meals.dinner: Dinner included as part of the Fado Show experience in Alfama, featuring traditional Portuguese dishes and regional wines in a historic, intimate Fado house setting.

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer is strongly recommended for a seamless luxury arrival. Confirm hotel early check-in in advance if possible given the 13:00 landing. Comfortable walking shoes are essential for Alfama's steep, cobblestone streets in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Belém Historical Landmarks & Pastéis de Belém — depart by private car or historic Tram 15E to Belém. Begin with a guided visit to the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a breathtaking masterpiece of Manueline Gothic architecture built to honor Vasco da Gama's voyage to India. Explore the grand cloisters and ornate church interior with a knowledgeable private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Belém with a visit to the iconic Tower of Belém, standing sentinel on the Tagus River, and the Monument to the Discoveries. Conclude with the quintessential Lisbon ritual — a visit to the original Pastéis de Belém bakery (open since 1837) for freshly baked custard tarts dusted with cinnamon, still made from a secret recipe. Browse the MAAT (Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology) for a contemporary cultural contrast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon for a refined evening in the Príncipe Real neighborhood. Enjoy pre-dinner cocktails at a rooftop bar with panoramic city views before a leisurely dinner at one of Lisbon's celebrated fine dining restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — indulge in the hotel's premium breakfast spread featuring local cheeses, presunto, fresh pastries, seasonal fruit, and freshly brewed coffee.
meals.lunch: Solar dos Presuntos (Belém area) or a riverside restaurant in Belém such as Feitoria — a Michelin-starred restaurant at the Altis Belém Hotel offering stunning Tagus views and refined Portuguese tasting menus.
meals.dinner: Alma — a Michelin-starred restaurant in Chiado helmed by Chef Henrique Sá Pessoa, celebrating the soul of Portuguese cuisine with modern sophistication. Reserve the chef's tasting menu with wine pairing for a world-class dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: Belém is approximately 6–7 km west of the city center. A private car or taxi is most comfortable for a luxury experience. Jerónimos Monastery can be busy on weekends — a private guided visit with skip-the-line access is highly recommended. Book Feitoria or Alma well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Sintra Royal Palaces Day Trip — depart early by private chauffeur (approximately 40 minutes from Lisbon) to the enchanting UNESCO World Heritage town of Sintra. Begin with the fairytale Pena Palace perched dramatically on a forested hilltop, a riot of Romantic-era color and architectural fantasy. Explore the palace interiors and terraced gardens with a private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to visit the mysterious Quinta da Regaleira, with its Initiation Well, underground tunnels, and esoteric symbolism set within lush romantic gardens. Alternatively, explore the elegant National Palace of Sintra in the town center, with its iconic twin conical chimneys. Stroll through Sintra's charming village center and sample local sweets including travesseiros (almond and egg cream pastries) from the famous Piriquita bakery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lisbon by private transfer in time for a relaxed evening. Explore the vibrant LX Factory — a converted industrial complex now home to concept stores, galleries, and acclaimed restaurants — for a stylish Sunday evening experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure to Sintra.
meals.lunch: Tascantiga or Lawrence's Hotel Restaurant in Sintra — Lawrence's is reputedly the oldest hotel in Iberia and offers a refined, historic dining setting perfect for a premium lunch amid Sintra's palaces.
meals.dinner: A Cevicheria or Tasca do Chico in Lisbon — opt for A Cevicheria in Príncipe Real for a creative, ingredient-driven menu by acclaimed Chef Kiko Martins, blending Portuguese flavors with global influences in a lively, design-forward setting.

day_by_day.notes: Sintra's hillside attractions involve significant uphill walking or tuk-tuk/taxi rides between sites. A private driver who can navigate between palaces is a worthwhile luxury upgrade. Pena Palace sells timed entry tickets — pre-book online to avoid queues, especially on Sundays.

day_by_day.morning: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour — head to the iconic Mercado da Ribeira in Cais do Sodré for an immersive, curated food tour of Lisbon's celebrated Time Out Market. Guided by a local food expert, graze through stalls representing the city's best chefs and traditional producers — sampling bacalhau preparations, fresh seafood, artisanal cheeses, charcuterie, and regional wines. Learn the stories and history behind Portugal's most iconic ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mouraria Neighborhood Food & Culture Walk — transition to Lisbon's vibrant, multicultural Mouraria quarter, the ancient birthplace of Fado. Join a guided cultural walk through this historically rich neighborhood, visiting hidden corners, Moorish-era remnants, local tabernas, and community gardens. Meet local artisans and hear the living history of this deeply authentic district that contrasts beautifully with Lisbon's more polished tourist areas.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a premium wine and cheese experience at one of Lisbon's finest wine bars, focusing on rare Portuguese varietals from the Douro, Alentejo, and Dão regions. Follow with a late dinner at a sophisticated Lisbon restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast, or a local café experience — visit Café A Brasileira in Chiado, one of Lisbon's most storied literary cafés, for a bica (espresso) and a pastel de nata.
meals.lunch: Grazing and tasting throughout the Time Out Market food tour serves as a comprehensive and delicious lunch experience — no separate restaurant needed.
meals.dinner: Cervejaria Ramiro — Lisbon's legendary, beloved seafood brasserie operating since 1956. An institution for premium shellfish: tiger prawns, percebes (barnacles), clams, and the iconic prego (steak sandwich) to finish. Lively, authentic, and unmissable.

day_by_day.notes: The Time Out Market is best experienced on a guided tour to navigate the extensive offerings with expert context. Mouraria is most atmospheric in the afternoon when local life is in full swing. Cervejaria Ramiro does not take reservations — arrive early or expect a wait, which is part of the authentic experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the National Museum of Ancient Art (Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga) — Portugal's most important art museum, housing a world-class collection of Portuguese paintings, decorative arts, and artifacts spanning the Age of Discovery. Highlights include Nuno Gonçalves' iconic Panels of São Vicente and extraordinary examples of Manueline gold and silverwork. A private guide will bring the historical context to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely afternoon for personal exploration and luxury shopping in the Chiado and Príncipe Real neighborhoods. Visit concept stores, Portuguese fashion designers, and artisan shops specializing in hand-painted azulejo tiles, fine cork goods, and Portuguese ceramics. Enjoy a final afternoon passeio (stroll) along the Tagus waterfront or up to the Miradouro de Santa Catarina for sweeping city views. Optional: indulge in a spa treatment at the hotel to unwind before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Lisbon's finest table — a celebratory, memorable final meal showcasing the pinnacle of contemporary Portuguese cuisine, followed by a nightcap at a rooftop bar overlooking the illuminated city.

meals.breakfast: Extended hotel breakfast — take time to savor the full spread on your final morning, enjoying local specialties including queijo da Serra, smoked sausages, and freshly baked bread.
meals.lunch: Taberna da Rua das Flores or Zé da Mouraria — a light, authentic Portuguese lunch in a traditional taberna setting, sampling seasonal dishes and house wines in a convivial atmosphere.
meals.dinner: Belcanto — Chef José Avillez's two-Michelin-starred flagship restaurant in Chiado, widely regarded as one of the best restaurants in Portugal and among Europe's finest. The tasting menu is a poetic, technically brilliant journey through Portuguese culinary heritage reimagined for the 21st century. An unforgettable farewell to Lisbon. Reserve months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Belcanto reservations are extremely sought-after — book as early as possible, ideally at the time of trip planning. If departure is early the following morning, consider packing bags and arranging luggage storage with the hotel to keep the final evening stress-free. A private transfer to the airport can be pre-arranged for a seamless luxury departure.
